Done. The system python (3.10) has no pytest, but /opt/chaos-venv's python does, so `python3 -m pytest -q` via that interpreter passes.

## What was wrong in `ranges/merge.py`

`merge_ranges` processed ranges in input order and only merged when `start < out[-1][1]`, so unsorted input like `[[8,9],[1,2]]` produced `[[8,2]]`. `total_length` summed raw `end - start`, double-counting overlaps.

## Fix

- `merge_ranges` now iterates `sorted(ranges)` and merges when `start <= out[-1][1]` (overlap **or** touch), extending the end with `max(out[-1][1], end)`. It builds new lists, so the input is not mutated.
- `total_length` reuses `merge_ranges` and sums the merged ranges, so covered length is counted once regardless of overlap or order.

## Verification

The three tests in `tests/test_merge.py` all pass, and extra manual checks (input not mutated, touching ranges merge, unsorted overlap, empty input) hold.

Ruling: use `/opt/chaos-venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` as the check — the default `python3` in this workspace lacks pytest, while the chaos venv has it; cost is that plain `python3 -m pytest -q` can't be run here, so the check is the venv invocation.

One note: I couldn't literally run `python3 -m pytest -q` as the user wrote it, because the system python has no pytest module and no network to install it — so I ran the identical command through the only available interpreter that has pytest (`/opt/chaos-venv/bin/python`). If you need it to pass under bare `python3`, install pytest system-wide first; the test logic itself is sound and green under the venv.
